intro: Document vectors are comparable only when the same column means the same token in every row.
task: Build a sorted vocabulary and document-term count matrix from already tokenized documents.
requirements: documents is a nonempty Python list of lists of nonempty strings. Individual documents may be empty.
Preserve case and token spelling exactly. Sort the unique vocabulary using Python string order.
Return vocabulary as a string list and counts as a NumPy matrix with one row per document. If all documents are empty, return shape (n,0). Count every repeated occurrence.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Collect the vocabulary across all documents before allocating the matrix.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Do not lowercase inside this function: tokenization and normalization belong to an earlier, explicitly chosen step.

explanation: A bag-of-words representation ignores token order but keeps occurrence counts. Its shared vocabulary maps each token to a consistent feature column.
Sorting the vocabulary makes the output deterministic. Counting unique tokens per document would instead produce binary presence features and lose repetition information.
Compare two documents with the same tokens in different orders. Then repeat one token. Explain which change this representation can detect and which it cannot.
formula: counts[d,t] = number of occurrences of token t in document d
